extracted.intended_audience: Catholic faithful preparing for confession and instruction in the sacraments (including children and catechism students)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical and doctrinal instructions for preparing for, performing, and concluding a Catholic confession; additional guidance on penance, indulgences, works of mercy, and a basic definition of the Holy Eucharist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell circumstances that alter the gravity of a sin
rubrics_metrics.description: You have to tell any circumstance that really makes your sin much worse or less than it seems; all other circumstances you need not tell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only relevant circumstances should be mentioned; extraneous details will confuse you and waste the priest's time.

rubrics_metrics.name: If you cannot remember number of sins, report approximate number and frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: If we cannot remember the number of our sins, we should tell the number as nearly as possible, and say how often we have sinned in a day, a week, or a month and how long the habit or practice has lasted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give approximate counts, describe frequency and duration of habitual sins to help the confessor assess and advise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forgetting to confess a mortal sin without fault does not invalidate confession
rubrics_metrics.description: If without our fault we forget to confess a mortal sin, our confession is worthy, and the sin is forgiven; but it must be told in confession if it again comes to our mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between accidental forgetting (forgivable) and willful concealment (grave).

rubrics_metrics.name: Willful concealment of a mortal sin is a grievous offense
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a grievous offense willfully to conceal a mortal sin in confession, because we thereby tell a lie to the Holy Ghost, and make our confession worthless.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concealing a mortal sin in confession is equivalent to denying one's guilt before God; it increases guilt and must be avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation after willful concealment
rubrics_metrics.description: He who has willfully concealed a mortal sin in confession must not only confess it, but must also repeat all the sins he has committed since his last worthy confession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberate failure to examine conscience or prepare for confession can turn forgetting into concealment; preparation is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglecting examination of conscience can equal concealment
rubrics_metrics.description: If you willfully neglect to examine your conscience or make any effort to know your sins before going to confession, then forgetting would be equivalent to concealing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper preparation for confession is essential; do not go without effort to recall sins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not dwell on detailed recollection of past sins
rubrics_metrics.description: It is best not to dwell in thought upon any particular past sin with the time, place, and circumstances of its commission; but simply to remember in general that you have in the past sinned against this or that Commandment or virtue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excessive recollection can lead to temptation or scrupulosity; focus instead on amendment and avoiding future sins.

rubrics_metrics.name: General confession: when necessary, useful, or hurtful
rubrics_metrics.description: A general confession is the confession of the sins of our whole life or of a portion of our life. It may be necessary (when past confessions were bad), useful (retreats, preparation for sacraments, change of state), or hurtful (to scrupulous persons).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare longer for a general confession but avoid it if you are scrupulous; it helps see the state of the soul over a lifetime and resolve amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penance given after confession satisfies temporal punishment
rubrics_metrics.description: The priest gives us a penance after confession, that we may satisfy God for the temporal punishment due to our sins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penance demonstrates willingness to make satisfaction; perform priest-imposed penance first, you may add light penances but do not undertake severe penances or vows without confessor's counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: If you forget or cannot perform your penance, act promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: If you forget to say your penance, your confession is not on that account worthless; but you should say it as soon as possible, and in the manner your confessor directs. If you cannot perform the penance imposed, inform your confessor and ask for another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely completion or communication with confessor preserves the sacramental integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penance vs. Baptism: remission of temporal punishment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sacrament of Penance remits the eternal punishment due to sin, but it does not always remit the temporal punishment which God requires as satisfaction for our sins. Baptism remits both eternal and temporal punishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand the distinction: after Penance one may still need to satisfy temporal punishment (earthly penance or Purgatory).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of temporal punishment
rubrics_metrics.description: God requires a temporal punishment as a satisfaction for sin to teach us the great evil of sin, and to prevent us from failing again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporal punishment is medicinal and corrective, not merely punitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chief means of satisfying temporal punishment
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief means by which we satisfy God for the temporal punishment due to sin are: prayer, fasting, almsgiving, all spiritual and corporal works of mercy, and the patient suffering of the ills of life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are principal methods; fasting especially refers to Church-imposed fasts (e.g., Lent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spiritual works of mercy (seven)
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief spiritual works of mercy are seven: to admonish the sinner, to instruct the ignorant, to counsel the doubtful, to comfort the sorrowful, to bear wrongs patiently, to forgive all injuries, and to pray for the living and the dead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admonish only in specified circumstances (mortal sin, authority/influence, likelihood of improvement); comfort, counsel, patient endurance and prayer are directed to appropriate persons and ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporal works of mercy (seven)
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief corporal works of mercy are seven: to feed the hungry, to give drink to the thirsty, to clothe the naked, to ransom the captive, to harbor the harborless, to visit the sick, and to bury the dead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes historical/duty explanations (ransom of captives, hospitality, burial of strangers); Christians obliged to perform these works in one way or another and may support religious institutions that perform them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support charitable institutions according to means
rubrics_metrics.description: If religious communities or institutions perform works of mercy on our behalf, we are obliged on our part to give them the means to carry it on; therefore we should contribute according to our means to charitable institutions and all institutions that promote the glory of God and the good of our religion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial or material support is a legitimate way to fulfill corporal and spiritual works of mercy when one cannot perform them personally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entering the confessional: posture and opening formula
rubrics_metrics.description: On entering the confessional we should kneel, make the Sign of the Cross, and say to the priest: 'Bless me, Father'; then add, 'I confess to Almighty God, and to you, Father, that I have sinned.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with humility and the traditional formula to prepare the sacramental act.

rubrics_metrics.name: First things to tell the priest
rubrics_metrics.description: The first things we should tell the priest in confession are the time of our last confession and whether we said the penance and went to Holy Communion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives context for the confessor to assess what to ask and what penances or advice to give.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confess mortal sins since last confession and venial sins as wished
rubrics_metrics.description: After telling the time of our last confession and Communion we should confess all the mortal sins we have since committed, and all the venial sins we may wish to mention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have no mortal sin to confess, mention some past mortal sin (even if previously confessed) to deepen sorrow and certainty of a good confession; keep secret any sins accidentally overheard of others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer confessor's questions truthfully and clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: When the confessor asks us questions, we must answer them truthfully and clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Honesty and clarity help the confessor diagnose and prescribe suitable remedies; do not withhold information when asked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listen attentively to confessor's advice and follow it
rubrics_metrics.description: After telling our sins we should listen with attention to the advice which the confessor may think proper to give.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The priest acts as judge, father, teacher, and physician—follow his remedies and do not change confessors frequently without good reason so that he can know your soul and aid progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change confessors only for good reason; avoid false shame
rubrics_metrics.description: If there should be danger of your making a bad confession to your own confessor -- on account of some feeling of false shame -- then go to any confessor you please; never be so much attached to any one confessor that you would remain away from the Sacraments a long time rather than go to another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize access to the sacrament and truthful confession over personal attachment to a particular confessor.

rubrics_metrics.name: End confession by accusing oneself of all past sins
rubrics_metrics.description: We should end our confession by saying, 'I also accuse myself of all the sins of my past life,' telling, if we choose, one or several of our past sins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formula expresses a comprehensive intention of repentance; optionally name a past sin if helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renew Act of Contrition during absolution
rubrics_metrics.description: While the priest is giving us absolution, we should from our heart renew the Act of Contrition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All, especially children, should know this act well before going to confession; interior sorrow is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indulgence defined as remission of temporal punishment
rubrics_metrics.description: An indulgence is the remission in whole or in part of the temporal punishment due to sin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indulgences draw on the Church's treasury of merits (Christ, Mary, saints) and are distinct from the forgiveness of guilt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indulgence is not a pardon nor a license to sin; state of grace required
rubrics_metrics.description: An indulgence is not a pardon of sin, nor a license to commit sin, and one who is in a state of mortal sin cannot gain an indulgence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must be in the state of grace to gain indulgences; being in mortal sin nullifies merit of good works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two kinds of indulgences: plenary and partial
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two kinds of indulgences--plenary and partial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plenary = full remission of temporal punishment; partial = remission of part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements and disposition for a plenary indulgence
rubrics_metrics.description: A plenary indulgence is the full remission of the temporal punishment due to sin. Gaining a plenary indulgence requires proper dispositions: hate sin, be heartily sorry even for venial sins, and not have a desire for even venial sin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a plenary indulgence one must also fulfill prescribed acts (see works enjoined) and have interior disposition of detachment from sin.

rubrics_metrics.name: How the Church remits temporal punishment by indulgences
rubrics_metrics.description: The Church by means of indulgences remits the temporal punishment due to sin by applying to us the merits of Jesus Christ, and the superabundant satisfactions of the Blessed Virgin Mary and of the saints, which merits and satisfactions are its spiritual treasury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indulgences operate by the Church applying its treasury of merits; 'superabundant' means beyond what was necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions to gain an indulgence
rubrics_metrics.description: To gain an indulgence we must be in a state of grace and perform the works enjoined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works include visiting certain churches or altars, giving alms, saying certain prayers, etc.; for a plenary indulgence it is required in addition to go to confession and Holy Communion and to pray for the intention of the Pope (one Our Father and one Hail Mary suffice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Three basic ways to gain a partial indulgence (and other means)
rubrics_metrics.description: A partial indulgence can be gained by: 1) raising one's heart to God amidst the duties and trials of life and making a pious invocation, even only mentally; 2) giving of oneself or one's goods to those in need; 3) voluntarily depriving oneself of something pleasing, in a spirit of penance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial indulgences are also granted for reciting certain prayers (acts of faith, hope, charity, contrition), performing acts of devotion (Spiritual Communion), devoutly making the Sign of the Cross, or using blessed articles of devotion. Intention to gain the indulgence is required; making a general intention each morning will cover indulgences you do not know about.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intention to gain an indulgence is required
rubrics_metrics.description: To gain an indulgence you must also have the intention of gaining it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A general intention (e.g., each morning) suffices to gain indulgences attached to prayers or acts you perform later, even if you do not know the specific indulgence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Habitual confession facilitates gaining plenary indulgences when other conditions met
rubrics_metrics.description: All those who are in the habit of going to confession every two weeks are able to gain a plenary indulgence when they fulfill the other prescribed conditions for gaining a plenary indulgence, even when they do not know that they are gaining the indulgence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular confession, combined with sacramental communion and prayer for the Pope's intention and proper disposition, can obtain a plenary indulgence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding historical phrasing of partial indulgences (days/months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Partial indulgences were formerly designated by specific amounts of time (e.g., 'an indulgence of forty days'), which referred to an equivalence with early public penances, not literal time removed from Purgatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not interpret such phrases as literal days; they indicate the amount of temporal punishment remitted compared to early penances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of the Holy Eucharist and institution
rubrics_metrics.description: The Holy Eucharist is the Sacrament which contains the body and blood, soul and divinity of Our Lord Jesus Christ under the appearances of bread and wine. Christ instituted the Holy Eucharist at the Last Supper, the night before He died.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Eucharist is the same living body of Our Lord in a new form and is to be treated with reverence (doctrine rather than procedural rubric).
